quest.title: Woven Wishes
quest.description: At Ayaka's request, you and Paimon accompany her to prepare gifts necessary to meet "Tsubaki."
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x525, Mora x35475, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

chapter.title: The Whispers of the Crane and the White Rabbit

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Hm? This must be...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's a festival promotion.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, speaking of — we haven't been anywhere fun since we arrived in Inazuma!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did you want to go, Ayaka?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: N—No, what made you think that? Ahem... Festivals are a common occurrence here in Inazuma. We in the Yashiro Commission are very well acquainted with these sorts of customs.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Each season brings its own festival... and each festival, in turn, brings a fresh challenge to the task of maintaining public order...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: So, while festivals are undoubtedly joyous and lively occasions, for us they are also a cause for concern...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Oh! My apologies, I should stop thinking about work, this is hardly relevant to the matter at hand. This store here is the place I wanted to visit.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, so you weren't checking out the promotion... Well, let's take a look inside then.

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: Welcome, I have all the latest styles. Please take a look!

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: Oh! It's Miss Kamisato — with guests from overseas! Welcome to Ogura Textiles & Kimonos. Are you here to purchase fabric, or for tailored garments?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Oh! Greetings to you too. I have a design here for a garment, would you be so kind as to take a look?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohh, Ayaka came prepared!

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: Let me see... Hmm? Hmm, this could be...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm? Could be...?

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: —Oh, it's a very fine design!

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: ...Miss Kamisato — you'd like us to make a kimono following this design, yes?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Please, if you could.

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: I'm honored that you'd choose Ogura Textiles & Kimonos for your tailoring needs! However... there is one rather difficult problem...

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: Based on the design, this kind of kimono would require silk made from the Silk Flower. The majority of Inazuma's silk is imported from Liyue Harbor, but given the current climate...

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: *sigh* As you well know, Inazuma is currently under a strict lockdown.

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: In all honesty, the impact on the textiles industry has been quite significant. We're struggling to import high-grade fabrics, so much of our tailoring business has been put on hold indefinitely.

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: But of course, where our customers are able to provide the fabric themselves, we can still be of service.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *sigh* So you're saying, we need to go and buy some silk first?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: If even Ogura Textiles & Kimonos can't get ahold of high-grade fabric... where would we buy it from?

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: You could try the International Trade Association. They are a little better connected than we are — after all, the association brings together merchants from all over the world.

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: The only thing is their prices... they're not the cheapest. In times like these, though, we're lucky to even have an option of getting hold of the things we want in the first place.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, so even just getting clothes made is an ordeal in Inazuma...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, the International Trade Association? That's Kurisu's thing, right? We haven't been to Ritou in a while.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Hmm... It looks like that will be our next stop.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Thank you ever so much. We will be back once we've acquired the fabric.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: In the meantime, I have one other very small request. Could you...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why's she being so secretive all of a sudden?

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm... Absolutely.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Much obliged.

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: My pleasure, Miss Kamisato.

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: Honestly, I'm just as excited as you to see the end product! We haven't made a silk kimono for the longest time now, and this is a beautiful design...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: That's very kind of you, thank you. Goodbye for now.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Traveler, Paimon — let's try our luck at the International Trade Association.

talks.objective: Go to the International Trade Association in Ritou

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Stop, thief!

dialogues.speaker: Ronin
dialogues.text: Hah! You think you can get your stuff back with this bunch? You must be dreaming.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Why you... You better hope you have the courage of your convictions...

dialogues.speaker: Ronin
dialogues.text: Why wouldn't I, old man? Answer me this — you're one of those outlander merchants, right?

dialogues.speaker: Ronin
dialogues.text: You trade association types are worms, coming over to our land, leeching off our people... Who's gonna leap to your defense, huh? Tell me, who's gonna stick their neck out for the likes of you?

dialogues.speaker: Ronin
dialogues.text: Hahaha! Look at that, no response. You know I'm right.

dialogues.speaker: Ronin
dialogues.text: Face it. This is Inazuma, you've got no ties here, you're at the bottom of the pile... Can you really blame us for walking all over you?

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: ...You are despicable...

dialogues.speaker: Ronin
dialogues.text: Hey! I just had an idea. Since you came all this way — how about we do some business?

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Business?

dialogues.speaker: Ronin
dialogues.text: Pay up, and you can take your fabric back. Sound good? If you ask me, it beats walking out of here with black eyes and a broken nose.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *gasp* You're just a big bully!

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: I... Ugh! What choice do I have...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Wait.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Mr. Kurisu, please do not pay any money to this man.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: But, but...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: I trust you remember our agreement? If you keep your lips firmly sealed, I, too, shall uphold my end of the deal.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Oh, yes, of course!

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Then please stand well back, where it is safe. Now... it is time for me to honor my word.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, that's that resolved then!

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: ...Phew.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: No, please, I... It was nothing, I was simply doing my duty.

response.speaker: Kurisu
response.text: Miss Kamisato, Traveler, a—are you hurt!?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Don't worry. We're fine.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: The vagrants left in quite a hurry — it would seem they didn't have time to take anything with them. I believe your stolen goods should all be here.

response.speaker: Kurisu
response.text: Th—Thank you, thank you so much...

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: You'd best do a count.

response.speaker: Kurisu
response.text: 6, 8, 10... Yep, it's all here!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Great! Now we can finally buy some silk!

response.speaker: Kurisu
response.text: Buy silk? ...You mean, you need some of this silk, here?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: This was indeed our intent.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't get us wrong though, that's not the reason we helped you out! Even if it were just a few Carrots or Cabbages, chances are we still would've helped you get them back.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon thinks we were pretty lucky! If we'd arrived any later, our chances of getting silk in Inazuma would have been zero...

response.speaker: Kurisu
response.text: I honestly can't thank you all enough...

response.speaker: Kurisu
response.text: Please, say no more! You need silk? I'll pick out a piece for you right away!

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Thank you, good sir. How much do I owe you?

response.speaker: Kurisu
response.text: Oh, it's free of charge! I could never ask you to pay after everything you've done for me!

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: No, no, that will never do. Things cost what they cost, and what they cost is what I shall pay.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Merchants already have enough challenges to deal with, and as Paimon explained, my help was unconditional. Please, sell your wares to me at the price you would sell them to any other customer.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: There is nothing to feel distressed about, because nothing, I repeat, nothing, happened here in these woods today. Did it?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Nope, just an uneventful stroll in the woods.

response.speaker: Kurisu
response.text: Thank you, I... I don't think I could ever repay you. You have helped me greatly, and I will never forget it.

response.speaker: Kurisu
response.text: I'm afraid we must part ways — I must get these goods back to the Association. If you ever need anything at all, just come to the International Trade Association and ask for Kurisu!

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Very well, and thank you for the silk, Mr. Kurisu.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: See ya then, bye! Safe journey home, don't go getting robbed again!

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Traveler, thank you for stepping in to help out.

choices.text: No worries, it's what I signed up for.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But... how come those vagrants didn't seem to know who you were? They must move in completely different circles, maybe they've never seen anyone from the Kamisato Clan before?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Perhaps. Either way, I'm glad they didn't recognize me. The fewer people who know what happened today, the better.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hee-hee, it's not every day an important person like you helps out someone like Kurisu. It really shows what a great person you are.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Oh, uh... Your praise is quite unwarranted. I merely did what anyone in my position would have done...

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: I admit that it did feel strange for me to come to his aid... But this should have nothing to do with identity, or social class... As far as I'm concerned, it was one individual helping another in need.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: I guess that deep down... I don't see how a society can be considered just when people encounter such obstacles in their livelihoods...

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Ah! Sorry, I'm getting off topic.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: No problem.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Right. Let's head back to Ogura Textiles & Kimonos and give our hard-won silk to the shopkeeper.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay!

choices.text: You made that look so easy!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look, look! There he is!

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Ah, looks like we found him.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: *whimpering* What am I going to do...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Mr. Kurisu, are you alright?

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Oh! You're M—Miss Ayaka from the K—Kamisato Clan. How do you do?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Better than you, it appears.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: And if it isn't the Traveler... I haven't seen you in a while — I take it you've been out of Ritou?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It sure has been a bit.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Thanks again for your help last time. The Association is back in business, and it's all thanks to you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's great, but uh... Why were you staring into space just now? Did something bad happen?

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Well... You see... *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: It's embarrassing to admit, but some of the Association's goods have been... stolen. By vagrants.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Which goods were stolen?

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: It was a batch of high-grade silk.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: We imported a big batch of silk from Liyue several years ago. It's been sitting in storage ever since.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Recently, we heard that clothing stores in the city have more or less sold off all their silk stocks. So we figured now would be a good time to bring our batch out of storage, thinking it'd probably fetch a good price. But then...

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: The vagrants swiped the whole batch then disappeared into the woods. I'd report it to the authorities, but...

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Well, as you know, they don't think much of foreign merchants like us. The Kanjou Commission don't want to give us the time of day — honestly, you can just tell that our suffering amuses them...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: While I also take issue with aspects of the Kanjou Commission's operational methods, please remember, Mr. Kurisu, that while you are here in Inazuma, you should be careful with your words.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Oh! M—My apologies... I had to let off some steam...

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Anyway, there doesn't seem to be much we can do ourselves to get our goods back.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: *sigh* Perhaps I'm doomed to go bankrupt after all...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: I'm afraid I can't intervene in an official capacity... but I can still help you get your lost goods back.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Of course, I would never— Wait, what!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Seriously?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Yes. Acting in my own capacity, mind you. Even then, there is no escaping the fact that my every action and word will be seen to reflect on the Yashiro Commission and the Kamisato Clan.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: I do so not without reservations, so... I hope that you will treat this matter as confidential.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: That aside — as I'm sure you're aware, I'm afraid that I won't always be able to help you in such circumstances.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Given your position and that of the International Trade Association... please try to exercise more caution in the future. You do not want to incur further unnecessary losses.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: We will, we certainly will!

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: But, um... are you sure this isn't going to cause any issues... for you?

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: What if someone high up in the Kanjou Commission sees what you're doing and doesn't like it? You're a highly respected member of society... Surely, putting your neck on the line for small-timers like me can't be worth the risk!?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Very humorous.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Let's not forget that I am the eldest daughter of the Kamisato Clan. I would be very surprised indeed if anybody in the Kanjou Commission felt that I was accountable to them for my actions.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, that sent shivers down Paimon's spine! Does everyone from a powerful clan talk like that?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Mr. Kurisu, I need to know the exact time and location of the theft, and anything that stood out about the perpetrators' appearance.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Thank you so much! Let's see, it was two hours ago now, over at the...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Everyone, please follow me to the scene of the crime. The investigation starts there...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, off we go!

talks.objective: Go to the scene of the incident to check out the situation
Talk to the ronin who snatched away the goods

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: Excellent news! So, apart from the silk, I think everything else I need, I've got in store already...

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: I just need to go and take stock of our materials — it won't take me a moment. I'll be right back.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They'd better be all there!

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: I do hope nothing else is missing.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Traveler, on the subject of garments, I've been meaning to acquire a new outfit for you, too.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: It's just... I wasn't sure how you'd feel about the idea of dressing in Inazuman attire...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's a kind thought, but I'm fine with my current outfit.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Oh? Are you sure?

choices.text: These clothes are special to me.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Is that so...

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Impressive... So, travelers of your stature hold themselves to a dress code, as well as a code of conduct.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... More like, when you're away from home, you've gotta live by certain rules to survive, whether you like it or not.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But Paimon would still love to check out some Inazuman outfits!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Do they do Paimon sizes here?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Just what is that supposed to mean? They make them in whatever size the customer asks for!

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Hahaha, ah, your interactions are so adorable to watch... Ahem! I mean, um... I can certainly find someone to tailor a Paimon-sized outfit, if Paimon so wishes.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Hm, well if you're sure... As you wish.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Something else I've been wondering is... how do people in other nations dress?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's so true — people dress in all kinds of ways!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Some people like to wear a hood, some cover up half their face with a mask, some just straight-up dress like a peacock... Oh, and some have their tummy on show, others wear skin-tight leotards and leggings... If you can imagine it, Paimon guarantees that someone out there is wearing it!

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Really? So there is no single standard, and people just dress however they like?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: So fascinating... Somehow, I feel a little envious...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, so you wanna dress like a peacock now?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: No, of course not! I—I just mean... I admire those who are able to do as they please.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: I would very much like to travel across the seven nations... and see how people live.

response.speaker: Ogura Mio
response.text: Sorry to keep you waiting! I've checked my inventory.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Thank you, is there anything else you're missing?

response.speaker: Ogura Mio
response.text: Fortunately not! I have all the materials I need. As for the size — would you like me to go by the dimensions given on the design?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Yes please.

response.speaker: Ogura Mio
response.text: Understood, I'll get to work shortly. In total, that'll be... this much!

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Here you go. Is it possible to treat this as an urgent order?

response.speaker: Ogura Mio
response.text: Well, luckily, we don't have any other urgents at the moment, so I can begin work right away. It will still take me some time, though, so please come and collect it later.

response.speaker: Ogura Mio
response.text: Until then, I'm sure you'll find somewhere nearby to pass the time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Good idea! Let's check out the whole area, we don't wanna leave any loose ends.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Haha, there will be no loose ends while you're in my company. I already decided where to go while we wait.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: For our next stop, I'd like to take you both for a meal.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Fooood! Ooh, Paimon likes this plan!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Perfect, I'm getting a little hungry myself.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Mm-hmm, I picked the venue especially for you — a humble local eatery called Kiminami Restaurant.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: I thought that the relaxed atmosphere there would suit our day much better than the prohibitively formal one of a high-end restaurant.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Shall we head off?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup yup, Paimon can't wait!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: They sure do! Each nation has its own unique style — traditional, fancy-schmancy, casual... All very different, but each style is suited to its region.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: The study of clothing is a profound discipline, and I have much still to learn.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: When clothing becomes part of the expression of one's personality, even an extension of one's body... That is quite a wonderful thing.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: So I am not against dressing up, far from it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon agrees! You couldn't have put it any better!

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Paimon, you're so adorable that you could wear anything and it would look lovely on you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow! Hee-hee, Paimon just got a compliment!

choices.text: Thanks, but Paimon and I are fine as we are.
If I'm too concerned about my appearance, I'll lose my edge in battle.

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: I do hope you manage to get hold of your silk.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there, we're back!

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: Welcome back!

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: So, any luck at the International Trade Association? Did they have any silk in stock?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Yes, they did.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Here.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: This is it, the International Trade Association.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, then... we need to talk to Kurisu, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Doesn't look like he's here. Let's look around!
